title: Lender Preflight Coordination
name: Lender Preflight Coordination
metaTitle: Lender Preflight Coordination in San Diego, CA
metaDescription: Lender preflight coordination for San Diego exchanges, checking rate-lock timing and underwriting conditions against the 180-day deadline before you rely on a quote.

sections.html: A financing quote for a San Diego replacement property usually comes with a rate and a rough timeline, and neither of those is guaranteed to hold up against a 180-day exchange deadline once underwriting actually starts. Lender preflight coordination means checking the lender's real conditions, appraisal timing, and rate-lock window against the exchange calendar before you count on that quote closing anything.

sections.heading: What a Rate Quote Doesn't Tell You About Timing
sections.html: A lender's initial quote is usually indicative, not committed, and the rate-lock period behind it is often shorter than the time it will actually take to clear underwriting on a San Diego commercial property. If the lock expires before closing, you are re-pricing at whatever the market has done in the meantime, which can change the numbers on a deal that looked settled weeks earlier. Ask for the actual lock period and underwriting timeline in writing, beyond the headline rate.

sections.heading: Why This Matters More in a Tight Market
sections.html: San Diego's constrained inventory across industrial, office-lab, and coastal multifamily means replacement candidates often move fast, and a financing delay can cost you the property even if the rate itself was competitive. A lender preflight check confirms the loan is genuinely ready to close on the timeline the deal requires, rather than merely priced attractively on a term sheet.

sections.heading: Where Appraisal Timing Becomes the Bottleneck
sections.html: Commercial appraisals on specialized property, life-science lab buildouts near UTC and Torrey Pines in particular, can take longer than a standard commercial appraisal because there are fewer directly comparable transactions to draw from. If the appraisal slips, the whole closing calendar slips with it, regardless of how ready every other part of the file is.

sections.heading: The Preflight Checklist Run Against Every Lender File
sections.html:
Before a financing quote gets relied on for a San Diego replacement closing, we confirm:

  • Rate-lock period against the projected closing date
  • Appraisal order date and expected turnaround
  • Underwriting conditions still outstanding
  • Loan-to-value and debt-service terms against the exchange budget
  • Payoff figure timing on the relinquished property loan, if applicable

sections.heading: What Stays With the Lender and Your Advisors
sections.html: Preflight coordination surfaces timing risk early. It does not replace the lender's own underwriting decision or your accountant's review of how the financing terms affect your exchange numbers. Confirm final loan terms directly with the lender before you rely on a preflight check as a substitute for a signed commitment.

sections.heading: Comparing Two Lenders Quoting the Same Rate
sections.html:
Two lenders can quote an identical rate on a San Diego replacement property and still carry very different closing risk, one with a rate lock that expires in thirty days and a streamlined underwriting file, the other with a sixty-day lock but a longer list of outstanding conditions. Comparing lenders on rate alone misses the variable that actually determines whether financing is ready when the exchange deadline arrives.

We ask each lender for the same set of details, lock expiration, conditions still outstanding, and appraisal order status, so a side-by-side comparison reflects real closing readiness rather than just the number on the term sheet.

That comparison also has to account for how each lender handles a rate-lock extension if closing slips, since the fee and terms for extending a lock vary widely and can erase whatever advantage the original quote appeared to offer.

A lender who is upfront about extension costs before a rate is locked is generally easier to work with than one who only discloses those terms after a closing date has already slipped past the original lock expiration.

Getting these details in writing early, rather than relying on a verbal assurance from a loan officer, is what actually protects the closing timeline against a rate environment that can shift over the course of a multi-month exchange.

A written record of extension terms also gives you something concrete to negotiate against if a delay turns out to be the lender's own underwriting backlog rather than anything on the borrower's side.

That documentation becomes especially useful if a rate-lock dispute arises close to the exchange deadline, when there is no time left to sort out verbal disagreements about what was originally promised.

Investors who skip this step tend to find out the hard way, usually in the final two weeks before closing, that the quote they budgeted around never actually reflected the lender's real underwriting timeline.

faqs.q: Is a lender's initial rate quote the same as a locked rate?
faqs.a: Usually not. Most initial quotes are indicative, and the actual lock period often starts later and runs shorter than the time needed to clear underwriting on a San Diego commercial deal.

faqs.q: Why does financing risk matter more in a tight market like San Diego?
faqs.a: Because a financing delay can cost you the replacement property entirely if another buyer is ready to move faster, even when the rate you were quoted was competitive.

faqs.q: Why do life-science lab buildings take longer to appraise?
faqs.a: Specialized property near UTC and Torrey Pines has fewer directly comparable sales, which can extend appraisal turnaround and, with it, the whole closing timeline.

faqs.q: What should I ask a lender before relying on their quote for exchange timing?
faqs.a: The exact rate-lock period, the expected appraisal turnaround, and any outstanding underwriting conditions, all measured against your specific closing date, not a general estimate.

faqs.q: Does lender preflight coordination replace loan underwriting?
faqs.a: No. It surfaces timing and conditions risk early so you and the lender can address it before closing. The lender still makes the final underwriting decision.
